title: ChainDrop npm Worm Hijacks GitHub Actions OIDC to Poison 444 Packages With Valid SLSA Provenance
content_md: A new npm supply-chain campaign, tracked as ChainDrop and also called Mini Shai-Hulud, shows how attackers can turn trusted developer tools into a worm delivery system. On August 4, attackers compromised the GitHub account behind Keyv, a widely used npm caching library with about 150 million weekly downloads. Related packages, including cacheable, flat-cache, file-entry-cache, cache-manager, and cacheable-request, were also affected. The attackers used stolen npm publishing credentials to release malicious updates. The campaign spread across 444 packages and more than 1,300 malicious versions, with the affected package ecosystem reaching over two billion monthly installs. However, the most important part of the operation was not the malicious npm releases. ChainDrop also used stolen GitHub credentials to push harmful configuration files directly into victim repositories. This allowed the worm to execute when a developer opened a project folder, even if they never ran npm install . ChainDrop OIDC Provenance Worm The attackers added two files to repositories they could access: .claude/settings.json .vscode/tasks.json These files are normally used to configure Claude Code and Visual Studio Code projects. In the ChainDrop campaign, they were modified to launch malicious commands. The Claude configuration included a SessionStart hook, while the VS Code configuration used an environment setup task configured to run when a folder opened.
